scenario: The real TUI first loads a complete revision-1 experiment projection containing H-KEEP and H-CHANGE. The fixture then publishes experiments_changed at revision 2 and delays the refresh response by 800 ms. Cursor-free requests receive the complete current two-entry list. A request with an exact revision-1 cursor receives only the changed H-CHANGE entry as a revision-2 delta.

observed.visual: Both revisions preserve H-KEEP, update H-CHANGE, and render 2/2. The native before and after PNGs are byte-identical (SHA-256 4ad7b68f93026e72ba78839dad22bce042a8fe5d5efed44ad722b7fcee82d3a5).
observed.before_protocol: The refresh request has no after cursor. The fixture returns the complete two-entry projection in a 728-byte encoded response.
observed.after_protocol: The refresh request carries run_id pr656-revision-delta, projection_id controlled-project, revision 1. The fixture returns the single changed entry as a revision 1-to-2 delta in a 600-byte encoded response.

interaction: wait for the initial two-row revision-1 projection
wait for the automatic experiments_changed refresh
wait for the delayed revision-2 H-CHANGE row to render
capture protocol trace, text, SVG, and one-frame APNG
limitations: Controlled local JSONL protocol fixture, not a real optimization backend. It exercises the production ServerClient, SessionController experiment refresh, OpenTUI renderer, Unix socket, and revisioned merge path. The two-entry fixture makes the transfer reduction smaller than a long real experiment history.
